tools.name: ffmpeg_doctor
tools.description: Report the installed FFmpeg and FFprobe versions, the configured executable paths, and which common encoders are present.

options.instructions: Call ffmpeg_doctor before a media job when FFmpeg may be missing or you need to know whether a codec such as libx265, libsvtav1 or h264_nvenc is available.

tools.name: ffmpeg_probe
tools.description: Inspect a media file with ffprobe: container, duration, bit rate and every stream with its codec, resolution, frame rate, sample rate and channels.

options.instructions: Always probe a file before transforming it. Use the real duration, resolution and codecs you received instead of assuming them.

tools.name: ffmpeg_convert
tools.description: Transcode one media file to another codec, container, resolution or frame rate. Creates the output; never modifies the input.

options.instructions: Use ffmpeg_convert for codec, container, size and frame-rate changes. Prefer libx264 + aac for compatibility and libx265/AV1 for smaller files. Keep the input path out of the output path so the original is preserved.

tools.name: ffmpeg_trim
tools.description: Cut one segment out of a media file. `copy` is fast and keyframe-aligned; `encode` is frame-accurate. Creates a new file.

options.instructions: Use copy mode for a fast cut, but the cut lands on a keyframe, so the start can be off by a few frames. Use encode mode when the exact frame matters.

tools.name: ffmpeg_extract_audio
tools.description: Extract or convert the audio track to mp3, aac/m4a, wav, flac, opus or ogg, with optional loudness normalisation.

options.instructions: Use wav or flac when the audio will be edited further; mp3 or aac when it will be played. Set normalize for speech that should sit at a consistent loudness.

tools.name: ffmpeg_thumbnail
tools.description: Write one still image from a video at a chosen timestamp (png, jpg or webp), optionally scaled.

options.instructions: Pick a timestamp that is inside the video, and probe first when you are unsure of the duration. A timestamp past the end produces no frame.

tools.name: ffmpeg_gif
tools.description: Turn a section of a video into a looping GIF with a generated colour palette (two-pass). Creates the GIF.

options.instructions: Use a short duration and a modest frame rate and width; GIFs grow quickly. 3 seconds at 12 fps and 480 px wide is a good default.

tools.name: ffmpeg_run
tools.description: Advanced escape hatch: run ffmpeg with an explicit argument list for an operation no other tool covers. Can overwrite files.

options.instructions: Reach for ffmpeg_run only for filters or muxing the structured tools do not cover. The structured tools are safer because they protect the input and validate the output. This tool adds -n unless overwrite is true.
